title: FSPL: A Meta-Learning Approach for a Filter and Embedded Feature Selection Pipeline
short_title: FSPL: Meta-Learning for Filter and Embedded Feature Selection

affiliations.b: Department of Computer Science Jerusalem College of Technology 21 Ha-Va’ad ha-Le’umi St., Jerusalem, Israel

journal: International Journal of Applied Mathematics and Computer Science
abstract: There are two main approaches to tackle the challenge of finding the best filter or embedded feature selection (FS) algorithm: searching for the one best FS algorithm and creating an ensemble of all available FS algorithms. However, in practice, these two processes usually occur as part of a larger machine learning pipeline and not separately. We posit that, due to the influence of the filter FS on the embedded FS, one should aim to optimize both of them as a single FS pipeline rather than separately. We propose a meta-learning approach that automatically finds the best filter and embedded FS pipeline for a given dataset called FSPL. We demonstrate the performance of FSPL on n = 90 datasets, obtaining 0.496 accuracy for the optimal FS pipeline, revealing an improvement of up to 5.98 percent in the model’s accuracy compared to the second-best meta-learning method.
summary: Machine learning models often work better when only the most useful input variables are kept, a step called feature selection. We argue that two common kinds, filter and embedded feature selection, should be tuned together as one pipeline, and we propose FSPL, a meta-learning approach (learning from experience across datasets) that automatically finds the best pipeline for a given dataset. Tested on 90 datasets, FSPL improved model accuracy by up to 5.98 percent over the second-best meta-learning method.
key_findings: Because filter feature selection influences embedded feature selection, the two should be optimized together as a single pipeline rather than separately.
